answer: Because the walnut cap is applied per key at the trellis settlement, the tide audit publishes each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces every alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. No single identity may earn more than 4647 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That is 33 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
